scope: Privacy-minimised consented-pilot evidence workflow and outcome aggregation

checks.evidence: The Pilot outcome workspace rendered structured identity, governance, review-effort, unit-economics, reference-accuracy, trust, and adoption controls.
A synthetic QA record saved with a verified event chain and the aggregate remained at zero evidence-eligible jobs and zero participants.
Consent and retention controls were disabled for synthetic QA and became available only after selecting Consented private pilot recording.
The browser rejected a consented-private save without an external consent record identifier; no evidence-eligible record was created.
Service tests rejected direct identifiers and free-text fields, and the aggregate suppressed participant, consent-record, source-hash, transcript, and audio details.
Per-job events formed a verified append-only hash chain and the dashboard reported the current structured record without copying transcript text.
The complete Docker dry-run suite passed after the pilot measurement implementation.

limitations: This verifies pilot controls and measurement infrastructure, not external adoption, dialect accuracy, trust improvement, or commercial outcomes.
No participant was recruited and no consent, retention, or publication authority is asserted by this test.
Small-cohort publication risk still requires owner review before sharing any real aggregate.
